whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical injury cases. That means your recovery isn't artificially boxed in by a statutory ceiling.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we win or settle your case. That structure lets you focus on healing instead of legal bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in La Puente?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involved a government entity, such as a city vehicle or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's best to talk with an attorney early so you don't lose your right to pursue compensation.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover damages even if you contributed to the accident. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than blocked entirely. An attorney can help assess how fault might affect your specific claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in La Puente?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors like Amar Road, Temple Avenue, Hacienda Boulevard, and Valley Boulevard, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 6 and 8 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.
